title: OSHA general industry lockout/tagout practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry lockout/tagout practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.147. Every answer is explained and linked to the rule text.

questions.question: Which of these types of employment does 1910.147(a)(1)(ii) list as outside the lockout/tagout standard?

options.A: Food processing plant employment
options.B: Construction and agriculture employment
options.C: Printing plant employment

questions.explanation: The list of what the standard "does not cover" begins with "Construction and agriculture employment".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: This standard does not cover the following: (A) Construction and agriculture employment;

questions.question: Work on cord and plug connected electric equipment falls outside 1910.147 when the hazard is controlled in which way?

options.A: By switching the equipment off at its on/off switch
options.B: By hanging a warning tag on the cord
options.C: By unplugging it, with the plug given to the shift supervisor to hold
options.D: By unplugging it, with the plug under the exclusive control of the employee doing the servicing

questions.explanation: The exception applies when exposure "is controlled by the unplugging of the equipment from the energy source and by the plug being under the exclusive control of the employee performing the servicing or maintenance."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Work on cord and plug connected electric equipment for which exposure to the hazards of unexpected energization or start up of the equipment is controlled by the unplugging of the equipment from the energy source and by the plug being under the exclusive control of the employee performing the servicing or maintenance.

questions.question: Servicing that takes place during normal production operations is covered by 1910.147 when which of these is true?

options.A: An employee is required to remove or bypass a guard or other safety device
options.B: The servicing is done by an outside contractor
options.C: The machine has run for more than eight hours that day
options.D: The operator asks for a lockout

questions.explanation: Servicing during normal production operations is covered only if "an employee is required to remove or bypass a guard or other safety device" or must place part of his or her body into the point of operation or an associated danger zone.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (A) An employee is required to remove or bypass a guard or other safety device; or

questions.question: Which of these is an energy isolating device under the definition in 1910.147(b)?

options.A: A push button
options.B: A selector switch
options.C: A line valve

questions.explanation: The definition lists devices including "a line valve; a block", and states that "Push buttons, selector switches and other control circuit type devices are not energy isolating devices."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: a line valve; a block; and any similar device used to block or isolate energy. Push buttons, selector switches and other control circuit type devices are not energy isolating devices.

questions.question: Under the definitions in 1910.147, when does an affected employee become an authorized employee?

options.A: After one year of operating the machine
options.B: When the employee's name appears on a tag hung by someone else
options.C: When that employee's duties include performing servicing or maintenance covered under the section
options.D: When a supervisor is watching the employee

questions.explanation: "An affected employee becomes an authorized employee when that employee's duties include performing servicing or maintenance covered under this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An affected employee becomes an authorized employee when that employee's duties include performing servicing or maintenance covered under this section.

questions.question: If an energy isolating device is not capable of being locked out, what must the employer's energy control program use?

options.A: A tagout system
options.B: Only the machine's stop button
options.C: A verbal warning to coworkers

questions.explanation: "If an energy isolating device is not capable of being locked out, the employer's energy control program under paragraph (c)(1) of this section shall utilize a tagout system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If an energy isolating device is not capable of being locked out, the employer's energy control program under paragraph (c)(1) of this section shall utilize a tagout system.

questions.question: After January 2, 1990, when new machines are installed, how must their energy isolating devices be designed?

options.A: With push-button stops in place of disconnects
options.B: With a holder for warning tags only
options.C: With a selector switch for each operator

questions.explanation: After January 2, 1990, whenever new machines or equipment are installed (or replacement or major repair, renovation or modification is performed), energy isolating devices "shall be designed to accept a lockout device."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: After January 2, 1990, whenever replacement or major repair, renovation or modification of a machine or equipment is performed, and whenever new machines or equipment are installed, energy isolating devices for such machine or equipment shall be designed to accept a lockout device.

questions.question: When a tagout device is used on an energy isolating device that is capable of being locked out, where must the tag be attached?

options.A: On the operator's control panel
options.B: At the same location that the lockout device would have been attached
options.C: On the main entrance door to the work area

questions.explanation: "the tagout device shall be attached at the same location that the lockout device would have been attached," and the employer must show the tagout program gives a level of safety equivalent to lockout.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When a tagout device is used on an energy isolating device which is capable of being locked out, the tagout device shall be attached at the same location that the lockout device would have been attached, and the employer shall demonstrate that the tagout program will provide a level of safety equivalent to that obtained by using a lockout program.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the items 1910.147(c)(4)(ii) says the energy control procedures must include?

options.A: Specific requirements for testing a machine or equipment to verify the effectiveness of lockout devices, tagout devices and other energy control measures
options.B: The production quota for the machine
options.C: The purchase price of each lock

questions.explanation: The listed items include "Specific requirements for testing a machine or equipment to determine and verify the effectiveness of lockout devices, tagout devices, and other energy control measures."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (D) Specific requirements for testing a machine or equipment to determine and verify the effectiveness of lockout devices, tagout devices, and other energy control measures.

questions.question: Tagout device attachment means must have a minimum unlocking strength of no less than how much?

options.A: 10 pounds
options.B: 50 pounds
options.C: 20 pounds

questions.explanation: The attachment means must be "non-releasable with a minimum unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Tagout device attachment means shall be of a non-reusable type, attachable by hand, self-locking, and non-releasable with a minimum unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds

questions.question: Lockout and tagout devices must be standardized within the facility in at least one of which criteria?

options.A: Price
options.B: Manufacturer
options.C: Weight

questions.explanation: Devices "shall be standardized within the facility in at least one of the following criteria: Color; shape; or size", and for tagout devices print and format must also be standardized.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Lockout and tagout devices shall be standardized within the facility in at least one of the following criteria: Color; shape; or size; and additionally, in the case of tagout devices, print and format shall be standardized.

questions.question: Under the "Identifiable" requirement, what must lockout and tagout devices indicate?

options.A: The date the device was purchased
options.B: The machine's serial number
options.C: The identity of the employee applying the device

questions.explanation: "Lockout devices and tagout devices shall indicate the identity of the employee applying the device(s)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Identifiable. Lockout devices and tagout devices shall indicate the identity of the employee applying the device(s).

questions.question: How often must the employer conduct a periodic inspection of the energy control procedure?

options.A: Every two years
options.B: Every three years
options.C: Every five years

questions.explanation: "The employer shall conduct a periodic inspection of the energy control procedure at least annually to ensure that the procedure and the requirements of this standard are being followed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall conduct a periodic inspection of the energy control procedure at least annually to ensure that the procedure and the requirements of this standard are being followed.

questions.question: Who must perform the periodic inspection of an energy control procedure?

options.A: An authorized employee other than the one(s) using the energy control procedure being inspected
options.B: The authorized employee who uses the procedure being inspected
options.C: Any affected employee who operates the machine

questions.explanation: "The periodic inspection shall be perfomed by an authorized employee other than the ones(s) utilizing the energy control procedure being inspected" (spelling as in the eCFR text).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The periodic inspection shall be perfomed by an authorized employee other than the ones(s) utilizing the energy control procedure being inspected.

questions.question: What must the employer's certification of a periodic inspection identify?

options.A: The hours of machine downtime and the cost of repairs
options.B: The names of the machine's suppliers
options.C: The machine or equipment, the date of the inspection, the employees included and the person performing it
options.D: Only the year in which the inspection took place

questions.explanation: "The certification shall identify the machine or equipment on which the energy control procedure was being utilized, the date of the inspection, the employees included in the inspection, and the person performing the inspection."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The certification shall identify the machine or equipment on which the energy control procedure was being utilized, the date of the inspection, the employees included in the inspection, and the person performing the inspection.

questions.question: Under 1910.147(c)(7)(i)(B), each affected employee must be instructed in what?

options.A: How to apply his or her own lock to the machine being serviced
options.B: The purpose and use of the energy control procedure
options.C: Nothing; only authorized employees receive instruction
options.D: Only the location of the first-aid kit

questions.explanation: "Each affected employee shall be instructed in the purpose and use of the energy control procedure." Under 1910.147(c)(8), "Lockout or tagout shall be performed only by the authorized employees who are performing the servicing or maintenance."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each affected employee shall be instructed in the purpose and use of the energy control procedure.

questions.question: Which event requires retraining for authorized and affected employees under 1910.147(c)(7)(iii)?

options.A: A new supervisor joining the department
options.B: The start of a new calendar year
options.C: A change in their job assignments

questions.explanation: "Retraining shall be provided for all authorized and affected employees whenever there is a change in their job assignments, a change in machines, equipment or processes that present a new hazard, or when there is a change in the energy control procedures."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Retraining shall be provided for all authorized and affected employees whenever there is a change in their job assignments, a change in machines, equipment or processes that present a new hazard, or when there is a change in the energy control procedures.

questions.question: Who may perform lockout or tagout under 1910.147(c)(8)?

options.A: Only the authorized employees who are performing the servicing or maintenance
options.B: Any affected employee who operates the machine
options.C: Any employee working in the area

questions.explanation: "Lockout or tagout shall be performed only by the authorized employees who are performing the servicing or maintenance."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Lockout or tagout shall be performed only by the authorized employees who are performing the servicing or maintenance.

questions.question: Under 1910.147(e)(3), apart from its stated exception, who removes each lockout or tagout device?

options.A: Any supervisor
options.B: The employee who applied the device
options.C: The next shift's machine operator

questions.explanation: "Each lockout or tagout device shall be removed from each energy isolating device by the employee who applied the device." The exception allows removal under the employer's direction only when the authorized employee is not available and specific documented procedures and training exist.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each lockout or tagout device shall be removed from each energy isolating device by the employee who applied the device. Exception to paragraph (e)(3): When the authorized employee who applied the lockout or tagout device is not available to remove it, that device may be removed under the direction of the employer, provided that specific procedures and training for such removal have been developed, documented and incorporated into the employer's energy control program.

questions.question: In group lockout or tagout, what must each authorized employee do when he or she begins work?

options.A: Sign a sheet kept by the crew leader instead of using a device
options.B: Hand his or her lock to the crew leader to apply
options.C: Rely on the operations lock alone
options.D: Affix a personal lockout or tagout device to the group lockout device, group lockbox or comparable mechanism

questions.explanation: "Each authorized employee shall affix a personal lockout or tagout device to the group lockout device, group lockbox, or comparable mechanism when he or she begins work," and remove it when he or she stops working on the machine.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each authorized employee shall affix a personal lockout or tagout device to the group lockout device, group lockbox, or comparable mechanism when he or she begins work, and shall remove those devices when he or she stops working on the machine or equipment being serviced or maintained.
